title: Poached Fish Florentine
description: Poached Fish Florentine is a classic Continental dish featuring delicately poached white fish served on a Florentine spinach base and finished with a rich Mornay sauce for an elegant restaurant-style presentation.

ingredients.title: Fish & Court Bouillon
items: White fish fillets (sole, halibut, or cod – skinless, boneless) – 800 g (200 g each)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Court Bouillon
steps: Combine water, white wine, onion, carrot, celery, lemon, herbs, peppercorns, cloves, and salt in a wide pan.
Bring to a boil, reduce to a gentle simmer, and cook for 20–25 minutes.
Strain, reserving the aromatic liquid for poaching.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Poach the Fish
steps: Return the strained court bouillon to the poaching pan.
Bring to 80–85°C (gentle simmer, never boiling).
Slide in the fish fillets carefully.
Poach gently for 6–8 minutes, until the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily.
Lift out fillets with a slotted spatula, keep warm. Reserve a little bouillon for thinning the sauce if needed.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Prepare the Spinach Florentine Base
steps: Blanch spinach briefly in salted boiling water, shock in ice water, then squeeze dry.
In a sauté pan, melt butter, add shallots, and sweat until translucent.
Add spinach, season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.
Cook just until tender and aromatic. Keep warm.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Make the Mornay Sauce
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan, stir in flour, and cook 1–2 minutes (no browning).
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth and slightly thick.
Add Gruyère and Parmesan, whisking until melted.
Season with salt, white pepper, and Dijon mustard (optional).
For elegance, pass sauce through a fine chinois for silkiness.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Assemble & Plate
steps: On each warm plate, spoon a neat bed of spinach (use a ring mold for precision).
Place a poached fish fillet gently on top.
Nap generously with Mornay sauce.
Garnish with microgreens or chive batons, serve with a lemon wedge.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Pair with a crisp Sancerre or Chablis.

chefTips: Temperature control: Gentle poaching avoids tough, dry fish.
Color balance: Shocked spinach ensures a vibrant green base.
Sauce refinement: Always strain sauces for a professional silky finish.
Plating: Use clean lines; fish centered, spinach as base, sauce draped with control (not drowning).
Wine pairing: A crisp Sancerre or Chablis complements beautifully.
